BAN ABORTION

Abortion is always a grave moral evil, and a woman who freely and knowingly procures one without coercion or ignorance is morally culpable of serious sin. However, the Church has never taught that this moral guilt automatically requires equal or mandatory civil prosecution in every case. Catholic moral theology has always distinguished between the objective sin, personal culpability before God, and the prudential role of civil law, which must act for the common good and may legitimately treat different participants differently. Scripture’s teaching that God shows no partiality does not abolish consideration of intent, freedom, and circumstances, nor does it require the state to impose identical penalties on all involved. By insisting that consistency demands criminal punishment of all women who obtain abortions, the abolitionist position replaces the Church’s long-standing framework of moral discernment, medicinal discipline, and prudential justice with a rigid legalism that goes beyond what true Christian teaching actually requires.

I agree that abortion is a grave moral wrong and that life is sacred. Scripture is clear on that.
But I’m cautious of any movement, on either side, that reduces this issue to legal absolutism without discipleship, mercy, and restoration.

God is both just and merciful. He hates the shedding of innocent blood and relentlessly pursues sinners with redemption. Jesus didn’t transform society by law alone. He transformed hearts, families, and culture. Laws matter, but culture is upstream from law.

If we don’t address fatherlessness, sexual immorality, trauma, medical deception, economic pressure, and the normalization of abortion through culture and pharmakeia, we won’t end abortion. we’ll just harden hearts and drive it underground.

Biblical justice is restorative, not merely punitive. That means defending life unapologetically while also offering accountability, support, truth, and a path to healing, for women, men, and families.
